question: Which offices may create, change and wind up a pension plan, enrol a member, record a contribution, issue a tax record and decide a benefit claim, which trustees or administrators hold that fiduciary authority, who may read plan funding figures, the enrolment list, retirement eligibility and the minutes of trustee meetings, and how is a member eligible to retire determined?
decision: Fiduciary acts require named plan trustees/administrator, plan authority and approved mandate; default none, so such writes are denied until configured and tested. Member reads are limited to own records; trustees see plan-wide records only under role and legitimate purpose. Do not issue pension tax documents or act on benefit claims until plan-specific rules, eligibility evidence and required registrations are verified; 501 is acceptable only for explicitly excluded launch capability.
originalProposedDecision: Fiduciary acts (plan changes, enrolment, contributions, tax records, benefit decisions) belong to the plan's named trustees or administrator, configured per org; default none, so writes stay 501. Members read only their own records. Plan funding, enrolment list, eligibility and trustee minutes: trustees and the plan administrator only.
independentApprovalScope: decision wording / platform baseline only; NOT independent security or operational testing
